title: Correcting an Adjudicated Claim Line on a Ridgecrest Advantage Plan by Reversal and Reprocessing
content:
A claim line already adjudicated under a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan is corrected by reversing that exact line and posting a corrected line in its place; the plan never edits an adjudicated line where the member's liability changes.

### Conditions of record

- The reversal names the single originally adjudicated claim line it applies to, and that line is on record with a claim status of paid, denied or adjusted. The member's claim history is the authority, tested before the reversal is posted and matched on the reference of the line being reversed.
- No reversal of that same originally adjudicated claim line is already on record. The same claim history is the authority; two reversals of one line are told apart by the date they were processed, and a second one is not posted.

### What the reversal carries

The reversal carries the negative of the member cost share the original line posted, so that the year-to-date accumulator returns to what it was before that line.

### After a favourable reconsideration

Where the correction follows a favourable reconsideration the corrected line is adjudicated at the cost share the decision directs, and any amount the member has already paid the provider above that figure is refunded to the member.

### Lines the member owed nothing on

A reversal of a line the member owed nothing on is still posted, at zero, so that the claim history shows plainly what the plan did.

### Line by line, never claim by claim

A whole claim is never reversed as one: each line is reversed on its own reference, because a claim number can cover several services with different outcomes.

*A claim number covers three services, of which one was denied and two were paid, and only the denied service is being corrected.* The reversal is posted against that one line on its own reference; the two paid lines are untouched.
